title: Introduce pocket-prefetch regulator and unit-economic CLI
author: Priya Desai
description: Motivation: customers running at constrained budgets need a lightweight, tenant-scoped prefetch controller that trades small increases in cold-start latency for measurable cost reductions and stable tail latency. This change adds a pocket-prefetch regulator service that applies budget-aware prefilling decisions, a small CLI to generate tenant-level unit-economic reports and recommended quantization/batching presets, and new telemetry to measure prefill cost vs. latency trade-offs. Key goals: (1) provide a low-risk opt-in controller for Dedicated/Private deployments, (2) surface unit economics so SREs and platform engineers can reason about cost/latency trade-offs, (3) enable automated safe rollouts with a canary policy. What changed: a) new service module prefetch/regulator implementing a percentile-based budget allocator and a short-lived prefill queue; b) policy DSL extension to allow 'pocket' budget rules per-tenant (prefill_budget_pct and tail_latency_slo); c) CLI command redwood unit-econ generate --tenant <id> that collects recent telemetry and recommends quant/batch defaults; d) telemetry: prefill_cost_scorer, prefill_tail_latency_p95, prefill_hit_ratio; e) small changes to admission logic to allow soft-prefill paths that can be degraded to on-demand when budget is exceeded. Rollout plan: merge behind feature flag pocket_prefill.v1 defaulted off; enable for internal staging tenants and run 72h smoke; if p95 latency regressions < 5% and unit-cost improves >= 8% we will schedule a gradual tenant opt-in by capacity. Checklist: - [x] design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/ENG-1219/pocket-prefetch-regulator-design - [x] unit tests for regulator allocator and CLI parsing - [x] integration smoke test for refill/degrade path - [x] observability dashboards updated - [x] feature flag gating implemented - [x] release notes entry drafted How to validate manually: 1) deploy with pocket_prefill.v1=true for a staging tenant; 2) run workload generator with mixed short/long sequences (templates in perf-lab/prefill-scripts); 3) run `redwood unit-econ generate --tenant staging-42 --output json` and inspect recommended batch/quant profiles; 4) compare /metrics for prefill_cost_scorer and prefill_tail_latency_p95. Backwards compatibility: all changes are feature-flag gated; default behavior unchanged. This is additive to the policy DSL and does not change runtime API shapes. Related work: touches prefill orchestration, telemetry composer, and the CLI surfaces used by platform engineers. Referenced Linear tasks and SUP ticket above.
